title: A2UI Atoms Catalog
description: The A2UI multi-surface atom vocabulary as an A2UI-v1.0 catalog document. Each stable atom is a component; a host resolves createSurface.catalogId (this file's URL) to it.
instructions: Every key under `components` is a valid `component` value (573 components). Compose layouts with Column/Row containers; each component's fields are its properties. Component envelope keys are `@`-prefixed in A2UI v1.0: `@catalogId` (set it on every component of this catalogue when the surface default is another catalog), `@metadata`, `@accessibility`, `@checks`; only `id` and `component` are unprefixed, and a plain `catalogId`, `metadata`, `accessibility` or `checks` is an ordinary component property. Canonical URI: https://a2uicatalog.ai/catalogue/a2ui-atoms-v1.json — full prose spec (descriptions, surfaces, attribution): https://a2uicatalog.ai/spec.json

sortable_list.description:
Drag to reorder a list, emitting the new position as one event.
A DATA atom, not a domain one: it renders whatever {id, label} pairs it is given and emits a position, so the same atom serves form fields, a shopping run, or any other AUTHORED ordering. There is deliberately no sortable_jobs and no sortable_fields — one named interaction per use case is the drift this vocabulary already has (onFlightClick, onAssign), and it costs a renderer change every time.
The reason it fits a declarative binding model at all is containment: the gesture never reaches the state engine. dragstart/dragover/drop are high-frequency and purely visual; only the DROP publishes, once, through the `onReorder` output wire as {id, order}. That is the same shape the atom renders FROM, so position is derived state rather than a second source of truth — what it emits and what it consumes are one field.
`order` is fractional: a drop takes the midpoint of its two neighbours, so exactly one item changes. Dense re-indexing would rewrite every position on every drag, turning a one-line reviewable diff into a wall of noise, which matters wherever the result is a change someone accepts or reverts.
Use it only where order is AUTHORED. Where order is COMPUTED — a job list ranked by severity then priority — a dragged position becomes a second, competing ordering, and the derivation boundary rule says that ranking belongs to the server.

items.description: array (required). Objects of {id, label, order?, group?, note?}. `id` is what comes back in the event, `label` is what is shown, `order` seeds the fractional position (defaults to the array index), `group` is an opaque bucket id carried back on drop, `note` is optional right-aligned secondary text.

label.description: string (optional). A small heading above the list.

emptyMessage.description: string (optional). Shown instead of the list when items is empty. Default "Nothing to reorder."

photo_grid.description:
A clickable image grid: every tile is both a photo and a row.
Built to close a real gap — data_table has no way to show what a row IS, only what it says about itself, so a photo-driven decision (which wallpaper, which chair) forced a text table plus a separate "View photo" link plus a separate select-then-tap-a-button flow before an action could fire. This atom is the shape that removes all three: the thing you look at and the thing you click are the same element.
Reuses data_table's onRowClick contract exactly — same data-row-json attribute, same _a2uiBindRowClicks binder, same array-wire form for "select AND immediately run an action" in one tap (shipped 2026-08-04 for onRowClick, inherited here for free rather than rebuilt). A DATA atom, not a domain one, same reasoning sortable_list gives for its own genericness: it renders whatever {id, url, ...} objects it is given and fires whatever the caller wired onRowClick to, so the same atom serves a voting board, a photo picker, or a product chooser without a second named atom per use case.
`badge` and `active` exist because a click-driven UI still has to show its OWN state back — a starred tile that does not visibly read as starred after the tap is a button that looks like it did nothing. Both are plain strings/booleans the caller derives server-side (a star count, a "you picked this" flag); the atom does not compute either.

images.description: array (required). Objects of {id, url, alt?, caption?, badge?, active?}. `id` is what data-row-json carries back to onRowClick (along with every other field on the object — the WHOLE row, same contract data_table's onRowClick already has). `caption` overlays the bottom of the tile. `badge` is a short string pinned top-right (a count, a status) — omit it for no badge. `active` outlines the tile and tints its badge to mark "this one is in a selected/chosen state" from the caller's own point of view.

cols.description: integer (optional, default 3). 2-4 reads best; more than 4 on a phone-width viewport crowds captions into illegibility.

photo_stepper.description:
A full-viewport, one-photo-at-a-time lightbox with prev/next and a vote button per slide — the sibling photo_grid does not cover: reviewing options ONE AT A TIME with full attention, immersively, rather than scanning a grid. Neither replaces the other; pick per use case, or offer both. Renders closed as a compact trigger card (first photo + label); clicking it opens the full takeover.
The takeover itself is a pure-CSS checkbox toggle — the SAME `#checkbox:checked ~ .overlay{display:...}` pattern the `css_modal` atom already uses for its own position:fixed;inset:0 overlay, not a new mechanism. Paging within the open overlay is the SAME pure-CSS radio-input trick the existing `carousel` atom already uses (sibling :checked selectors drive the slide transform) — no JS-tracked index to go stale, and critically, nothing for a live data refresh to disturb: `carousel` never had a live-update wire to worry about, but this atom does, and the radio's own browser-owned :checked state surviving a vote untouched is what stops "vote on photo 12, get silently bounced back to photo 1" from ever being possible in the first place — not a bug that was fixed, a failure mode the design does not have. Same reasoning protects open/closed state: the checkbox is the browser's own state too, so a live update cannot close the overlay out from under you either.
That is also why this atom's live-update path (_a2uiUpdatePhotoStepper) is NOT a rebuild like photo_grid's own _a2uiUpdatePhotoGrid — it patches each slide's badge/vote-button/voter-line IN PLACE, matched by candidate id (not array position), and touches nothing else. Matching by id, specifically, because the typical consumer of this atom (a live vote board) re-sorts its candidate list by vote count on every read while voting is open — so a candidate's position in the incoming array can move the instant ANY vote lands, including the one just cast on the slide currently open; patching by position against a reordered array would silently swap a different candidate's photo/name into the slide the radio's :checked state still has open. A consequence worth knowing before using this atom: because the update path patches EXISTING slide elements rather than creating them, the caller should populate the initial `images` prop with real data at render time (server-side), not rely purely on the `rows` wire to populate an empty first paint — an update arriving before any slide exists to patch has nothing to act on.
Reuses photo_grid's click contract exactly for the vote button (same data-row-json attribute, same generalised [data-row-json] binder in A2UIState.html) — the third consumer of a mechanism built once for data_table's own onRowClick.

images.description: array (required). Objects of {id, url, alt?, name?, price_display?, badge?, active?, starred_by_display?, source_url?}. Same shape family as photo_grid (id/url/badge/active carry the identical meaning), plus fields specific to a one-at-a-time review: `name`/`price_display` render as the slide's caption title/subtitle, `starred_by_display` is a plain pre-joined string (e.g. "Curtis, Marianne") shown under the caption, `source_url` (optional) renders a plain "Open source listing" link in the caption when present — the atom does not aggregate voter names or validate the link itself, the caller derives both server- side, same reasoning photo_grid gives for `badge` and `active` being caller-derived rather than computed by the atom.

accent.description: string (optional, hex, default #0f766e). Vote-button and active- badge colour.

trigger_label.description: string (optional, default "Browse full screen"). Label shown on the closed trigger card, next to the photo count.

preview_frame.description:
An iframe whose `src` is driven by a wire, so picking a value elsewhere on the page re-navigates it CLIENT-SIDE — no server round trip, no paint_result, nothing else on the page repainted.
A DATA atom, same spirit as sortable_list: it renders whatever src it is given and reacts to whatever is wired into it; it has no opinion on what the iframe shows. Meant to sit next to a picker (menu/select) and a StringTemplate primitive that turns the picked value into a URL — e.g. a "preview this before you commit it" panel, where committing is a SEPARATE, ordinary action.
Same-origin only in practice: nothing here relaxes sandboxing. A cross-origin src is subject to the embedded page's own frame-ancestors / X-Frame-Options exactly as any other iframe.

src.description: string (optional). Initial iframe URL. Empty renders the placeholder instead of an iframe. Normally left empty and driven entirely by `wire.src`.

label.description: string (optional). A small heading above the frame.

height.description: number (optional). Frame height in px. Default 320.

emptyMessage.description: string (optional). Shown in the placeholder before a src exists. Default "Nothing selected yet."

actual_vs_estimate.description:
A quantity carrying BOTH what is known and what is projected, each labelled, neither omittable. A data atom rather than a domain one: cost is only the first instance. The same shape holds for effort (hours worked vs hours estimated), for work items (closed vs open) and for anything else an app tracks with an actual alongside a forecast — which is most things worth tracking.
Exists because that distinction is where composed answers go wrong. Asked "what has this cost", a model resolves the ambiguity by guessing, and on 2026-08-14 presented a EUR300 estimate for unstarted work under the heading "COST". Selection prose can ask it not to; a required-field shape makes it unrepresentable. Both figures are mandatory for exactly that reason.
The contract runs in two directions, which is the point. Upward it constrains what a UI can say. Downward it tells the data layer what it must be able to produce: an app that cannot separate incurred from projected cannot fill this atom, and discovering that is the useful part.

actual.description: number (required). The known value, UNFORMATTED. Money spent, hours worked, items closed.

estimate.description: number (required). The projected value. Never fold this into `actual`; that is the error the atom exists to prevent.

unit.description: string (optional). Prefixed if it is a currency symbol ("EUR", "$"), suffixed otherwise (" hours", " jobs"). The renderer formats; the author supplies numbers.

show_total.description: boolean (optional, default true). The renderer DERIVES actual + estimate — the author never supplies it. A one-payload, one-render arithmetic belongs to the renderer under the derivation boundary rule, and an author who supplies a sum can supply a wrong one. Set false where adding the two is nonsense.

caption.description: string (optional). One honest sentence, e.g. "Nothing has been spent yet; EUR340 of work is planned."

accent.description: string (optional). Hex colour for the total.

sankey_flow.description: Renders a flow diagram (Sankey flow) where nodes sit in columns from left to right and are connected by curved gradient Bezier bands whose width is the flow value. Two or more columns; columns come from each node's optional `column` hint, or from graph distance when it is absent. Layout is d3-sankey's.

nodes.description: list of dictionaries (e.g., [{'id': 'revenue', 'label': 'Revenue', 'column': 0, 'color': '#10b981'}, ...]); `column` is an optional hint, an integer 0..n for the left-to-right column (0 = leftmost, up to 15); without it the column is the node's distance from the sources (a node with no outgoing flow goes to the last column), so a source -> middle -> target chain gets three columns and the chart is wider by 220px per column beyond two. Flows that close a cycle, or would run backwards between columns, are not drawn and are listed in a note under the chart.

title.description: string (optional, title of the chart, e.g., 'Financial Flow Allocation')

keyed.description: bool (optional, default false). True adds the build contract to the drawing so motion_build and motion_transition can move its parts: each node rectangle carries data-cb "node" and each node name data-cb "label", both with data-key = the node id, and each flow carries data-cb "link" with data-key = "sourceId>targetId" (a repeated pair gets "#2", "#3"). Use ids that another atom also keys (ISO 3166-1 alpha-3 codes against choropleth_map tiles) and a motion_transition joins the two element by element. Absent or false: the markup is unchanged, byte for byte.

weighted_words.description: Agentic typesetting: the agent decides how much each WORD weighs. A headline where every word carries an emphasis 1-5 that sets its size, weight and opacity, with the heaviest words in the accent colour; words land in sequence, heavier ones from higher up. The reader sees the shape of the argument before reading it. Give it "words" as [{text, weight}] to typeset deliberately, or plain "text" for an even setting. Screenshot-ready, light or dark. Capped at 40 words of 24 characters; weights clamp to 1-5.

animate.description: bool (optional). Words land in sequence on load. Default true.

stance.description: A claim whose typography IS its calibration. The agent states a claim and a confidence 0-1; the type sets itself from it -- weight from 300 (a hunch) to 900 (a conviction), size from 1.4rem to 3rem, tracking tightening and opacity rising with confidence -- under a thin confidence rail. Optional "because" (the reason) and "unless" (what would change the agent's mind, the line most opinion cards forget). A small slider lets the reader drag the confidence and watch the claim reset, which makes the mapping legible and honest. Same integer arithmetic on the server and in the slider script.

claim.description: string (required). The claim, up to 200 characters.

confidence.description: number (optional). 0-1 (values above 1 are read as percent). Default 0.5.

because.description: string (optional). The reason, one or two sentences.

unless.description: string (optional). What would change the agent''s mind; rendered as "I would change my mind if ...".

interactive.description: bool (optional). Show the try-it slider. Default true.

type_scale.description: A modular type scale, computed and shown as a specimen sheet. Declare a base size and a musical ratio (minor second through golden ratio) and the atom calculates every step -- px and rem to the hundredth, computed with the same integer-safe arithmetic on every renderer -- and sets the sample line at each size with a proportion bar, plus a ready-to-paste block of CSS custom properties. Calcs baked in, the way wall_elevation bakes in wall maths: an agent declares intent (base, ratio, steps), the atom does the typography. Light or dark, no JavaScript.

base.description: integer (optional). Base size in px, clamped 10-32. Default 16.

steps_up.description: integer (optional). Steps above the base, clamped 1-8. Default 6.

steps_down.description: integer (optional). Steps below the base, clamped 0-3. Default 2.

sample.description: string (optional). Sample line set at each size. Default "The quick brown fox".

show_code.description: bool (optional). Append the CSS custom properties block. Default true.

readability_card.description: Prose metrics as a typographic card: the Flesch reading-ease score set huge, its plain-language grade, and a stat row -- words, sentences, minutes to read at a declared words-per-minute, words per sentence, syllables per word, longest sentence -- all computed by the renderer from the text with identical arithmetic on every renderer (syllables by a vowel-group heuristic, sentences on . ! ? followed by space). The excerpt is shown underneath with the longest sentence highlighted, which is usually the one to cut. Built for the writing workflow; give it a draft and it tells you what a reader will feel.

contrast_audit.description: WCAG 2.1 contrast audit with the maths baked in: for each foreground/background pair the renderer computes the relative luminance and contrast ratio, shows a live sample swatch, and badges AA (4.5:1), AA large (3:1) and AAA (7:1) as pass or fail. Failing pairs get the nearest passing colour, found by mixing the foreground toward black or white in 5% steps until it clears AA. A summary line counts the passes. For an agent composing a surface this is the difference between "looks fine" and "is readable". No JavaScript; light or dark.

bg.description: "#rrggbb" (optional). Single-pair shorthand when pairs is absent.

label.description: string (optional). Label for the single-pair shorthand.

chartjs_bar.description: Draws a static, accessible bar chart as HTML (no script, no chart library) from labels and datasets, in grouped, stacked, relative or overlaid bars, vertical or horizontal, negative values, a linear or log value axis, d3 number formats, optional value labels and a legend. Series differ by fill pattern as well as colour, and a hidden table holds every value.

labels.description: array of strings. Category labels (up to 40 drawn; the hidden table lists all).

datasets.description: array of {label, data, color}. One series each (up to 8 drawn); data is numbers, anything else is skipped with a note; color is an optional

mode.description: group (default) | stack | relative | overlay. stack adds the signed values; relative stacks positives up and negatives down separately; overlay draws every series on the baseline.

show_values.description: boolean. Value labels on the bars; they hide when the chart is too narrow to fit them (the table keeps every value).

value_format.description: d3-format string for the value labels, for example ',.0f' or '.1%'. Types b c o p r x X are not supported.

y_format.description: d3-format string for the axis labels (and the value labels when value_format is absent).

y_scale.description: linear (default) | log. A log axis ticks at powers of ten, leaves out numbers that are not above zero (with a note) and cannot stack.

y_range.description: array of two numbers, min then max. Fixes the value axis; bars past it are cut at the axis with a note.

gap.description: number 0 to 0.8 (default 0.3). Share of each category slot left empty.

legend_position.description: top | bottom | right | none. Default top with more than one series, none otherwise.

version.description: integer (optional, default 1). Only version 1 exists; a higher whole number is drawn as version 1 with a note.

chartjs_bar.x-routing-text: Draws a static bar chart (no interactivity, no Chart.js) from labels and datasets. A phrase like 'how much you could save', describing one comparison figure rather than a full dataset, usually means actual_vs_estimate, metric_comparison_card, or stat_card, not this -- chartjs_bar is for a chart with several data points. If the request describes a single number or one comparison rather than a visual chart with axes and multiple data points, it is NOT this -- chartjs_bar needs an explicit request for a bar chart or graph.

chartjs_line.description: Renders an interactive line chart using Chart.js for time-series or trend data.

title.description: string (optional). Heading of the chart. With series it is drawn above the plot; the labels/datasets drawing in the web preview does not show it (the Apps Script renderer does).

series.description: (optional, preview) array of up to 8 series {label, x, y, mode, color, dash, shape, size, symbol, fill, text}. x is numbers or ISO 8601 date strings (UTC; a missing x is the index 0, 1, 2...), y numbers. mode lines|markers|lines+markers|text or any + combination (default lines+markers up to 20 points, else lines). color a #hex or colour word, else the theme palette. dash solid|dash|dot|dashdot|longdash|longdashdot, symbol circle|square|diamond|triangle-up|cross|x (both cycle per series when unset, so series differ by more than colour). shape linear|spline|hv|vh|hvh|vhv. size a diameter number or an array per point (bubble). fill tozeroy|tonexty. text an array of point labels. Present and non-empty, this replaces the labels/datasets (or data_points) drawing; absent, nothing changes.

x_type.description: (optional, with series) linear or date. Default: date when the first x is a date string, else linear.

x_label.description: string (optional, with series). Axis title under the plot. scatter_trend also reads label_x.

y_label.description: string (optional, with series). Axis title above the plot. scatter_trend also reads label_y.

max_points.description: (optional, with series) integer 50 to 2000, default 2000. A series with more usable points is thinned to evenly spaced points (first and last kept) and a visible note says so; the hidden table lists the drawn points. This is the scattergl case: many points, a cap, never a silent drop.

version.description: integer (optional, default 1). A whole number above 1 draws as version 1 with a note.

stacked_area.description: A stacked area chart: one coloured layer per series, stacked on a zero baseline over an ordered x axis (time, stages, categories), so the top edge is the total and each layer's thickness is that series' value. Drawn as SVG with a zero-based value axis, a legend and a hidden data table. The optional offset turns it into a 100% share chart (expand), a centred chart (silhouette) or a streamgraph (wiggle). Before 2026-10-21 the default was a list of horizontal bars; layout 'bars' still draws that.

labels.description: list of strings representing X-axis ticks (e.g., ['Q1', 'Q2', 'Q3', 'Q4'])

series.description: list of dictionaries representing stacked layers: [{'label': 'Enterprise', 'data': [10, 25, 45, 60], 'color': '#00f2ff'}, ...]

layout.description: string (optional, default 'area'): 'area' draws the stacked area chart (SVG, zero baseline, value axis). 'bars' draws a list of horizontal stacked bars, one row per label; that was the only drawing before 2026-10-21 and 'bars' keeps it unchanged. Absent, null or any other value means 'area'. The bar list ignores offset (a note says so when one is given).

offset.description: string (optional, area layout only): how the layers sit on the baseline. Absent, 'none' or anything else is the plain zero baseline. 'expand' scales every point to 100% (a 0-100% axis), 'silhouette' centres the layers on a middle line, 'wiggle' is a streamgraph (d3's wiggle baseline, layers ordered inside-out). silhouette and wiggle have no value axis (the baseline means nothing); the hidden table lists the raw values. Up to 12 series and 60 labels; negative or non-numeric cells draw as 0 and are counted in a note.

version.description: integer (optional, default 1). The stacked_area contract the payload was written for. Only version 1 exists; a higher whole number draws as version 1 with a note.

stacked_area.x-routing-text: A stacked area chart: how several series add up to a total over time or across ordered stages, with each series as a coloured layer. Use offset 'expand' for shares of the whole and 'wiggle' for a streamgraph. Not for a single line (use a line or sparkline atom), not for unordered categories (use a bar chart) and not for a table of values.

series.description: list of {label: string, color: string (optional hex, auto-assigned otherwise), points: list of {predicted: number 0-1, observed: number 0-1, n: integer (optional sample size, grows point radius), ci_low: number (optional), ci_high: number (optional)}}

scatter_trend.description: Renders a coordinate scatter grid representing discrete data points intersected by a prominent glowing linear regression line.

series.description: (optional, preview) array of up to 8 series {label, x, y, mode, color, dash, shape, size, symbol, fill, text}. x is numbers or ISO 8601 date strings (UTC; a missing x is the index 0, 1, 2...), y numbers. mode lines|markers|lines+markers|text or any + combination (default lines+markers up to 20 points, else lines). color a #hex or colour word, else the theme palette. dash solid|dash|dot|dashdot|longdash|longdashdot, symbol circle|square|diamond|triangle-up|cross|x (both cycle per series when unset, so series differ by more than colour). shape linear|spline|hv|vh|hvh|vhv. size a diameter number or an array per point (bubble). fill tozeroy|tonexty. text an array of point labels. Present and non-empty, this replaces the labels/datasets (or data_points) drawing; absent, nothing changes.

x_type.description: (optional, with series) linear or date. Default: date when the first x is a date string, else linear.

x_label.description: string (optional, with series). Axis title under the plot. scatter_trend also reads label_x.

y_label.description: string (optional, with series). Axis title above the plot. scatter_trend also reads label_y.

max_points.description: (optional, with series) integer 50 to 2000, default 2000. A series with more usable points is thinned to evenly spaced points (first and last kept) and a visible note says so; the hidden table lists the drawn points. This is the scattergl case: many points, a cap, never a silent drop.

version.description: integer (optional, default 1). A whole number above 1 draws as version 1 with a note.

motion_timeline.description: A stage of child atoms choreographed on ONE clock, the way a product or launch video is: everything on screen is a pure function of time (seek(t)), so it plays, loops, scrubs, and can be frozen on any frame (open the page with #t=3.2). Children are any atoms, placed in percent of a fixed-size stage (so the composition is identical at every width) and addressed by id; tracks animate them by opacity, x/y, scale, rotate, 3D tilt, blur, wipe, and two custom properties the demo kit listens to (p = progress, step = which caption/nav item); a camera track pans, zooms and tilts the world while layer:"hud" children (captions) stay put. Each key is a DESTINATION: {t, x, ease} means arrive at x at time t using ease, like GSAP .to(); before a property's first key it holds that first value, so an element can be hidden until its first key. Ease is a token name from motion_tokens (expo-out, standard, quart-in-out, overshoot, hold...) or four cubic-bezier numbers; with bpm set, keys take beat instead of t so the piece sits on a grid. Style that reads as designed rather than generated: one orchestrated moment per scene, entrances 600 ms or less on expo-out, on-screen moves on standard, the camera on quart-in-out, a shared motion vector between scenes, restraint over noise by default (no particle bursts, neon glows or bouncy easing on UI; the opt-in expressive options, glow, shine, trails and ripples, are for a film that wants them). Honours prefers-reduced-motion (holds the poster frame; controls still work).

title.description: string (optional, max 80). Accessible name of the stage. Default "Motion sequence".

aspect.description: "16:9" | "4:3" | "1:1" | "9:16" (optional, default "16:9"). The stage is laid out at 1280x720, 1200x900, 1000x1000 or 720x1280 logical px and scaled to the container.

bpm.description: integer (optional). 0-240. When set, keys may use `beat` (t = beat * 60 / bpm) instead of `t`.

ease.description: string | [x1,y1,x2,y2] (optional). Default ease for keys that do not name one. A token from motion_tokens (not "hold"). Default "standard".

autoplay.description: bool (optional). Plays when scrolled into view, pauses when it leaves. Default true. Off, or under prefers-reduced-motion, it shows the poster frame.

drive.description: "time" | "scroll" (optional, default "time"). "scroll" turns the film into a scroll-driven piece: the stage is pinned (position:sticky) inside a tall runway and the film clock is the page's scroll progress through that runway (seeked on requestAnimationFrame from a passive scroll listener), so scrolling plays the film and scrolling back rewinds it. No autoplay and no play/pause button: the scrubber stays as a progress indicator and a keyboard control (moving it scrolls the page to that point), and the page's own keys scroll as usual. Under prefers-reduced-motion there is no runway: the poster frame is shown in the normal flow. The export buttons are not offered. Absent or any other value: unchanged.

scroll_length.description: number (optional). With drive "scroll": the runway height in percent of the viewport height, clamped 150-1000, default 300 (the film plays over the runway minus one viewport of travel).

controls.description: bool (optional). Play/pause button, scrubber and clock. Default true.

poster.description: number (optional). Seconds; the frame shown when not autoplaying. Default 60% of duration.

transcript.description: bool (optional). Default false (nothing is added). True adds, under the stage, a "Transcript" disclosure (a details element, works without script) holding a table of every text and value the film shows, in reading order: time on screen (from the same keyframes as the player, the cue timing of film_to_vtt), scene (the scene layer it sits in), and the text. Covers motion_text, demo_caption lines, motion_counter, motion_pill, motion_checklist, demo_kpis, demo_chart (title, labels and values), demo_progress and demo_toggle_grid, nested or not. Up to 200 rows.

theme.description: "dark" | "light"  (optional, default "dark"). Stage background and control colours.

blocks.description: array (max 24) of any atom blocks. Each may also carry id (^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]{0,31}$, makes it addressable by a track), place {x, y, w, h, z, origin} (x/y/w/h in percent of the stage; z 0-99; origin "c"|"tl"|"t"|"b"|"l"|"r" is the transform origin), and layer "world" (default, moves with the camera) or "hud" (stays on screen).

tracks.description: array (max 40) of {target: id, keys: [...]} (max 48 keys each). A key is {t | beat, ease?, x?, y?, opacity?, scale?, rotate?, rx?, ry?, blur?, clip?, p?, step?, a?}. x,y are the element's top-left in percent of the stage (for an element nested in another, an offset from its natural place); opacity 0-1; scale 0-6; rotate, rx, ry in degrees (tilt -80..80); blur 0-40 px; the filter keys hue (degrees, -360..360), saturation, brightness, contrast (multipliers 0-4, 1 = unchanged) and invert (0-1) are composed with blur into one CSS filter on the element, clamped to those ranges, and the settled frame is the value at the last key (a brightness or invert track that swings quickly is checked as a possible flash by scripts/motion_lint.py); clip 0-1 is a left-to-right wipe; p 0-1 drives a demo atom's progress (chart draw, bar growth, toggles, fills, click ripple, orb level) and recounts its numbers; step is a float that crossfades captions and selects the active nav item. ease on a key is the ease of the segment ARRIVING at that key: a token name, "hold" (jump at the key), or four numbers. PATH FOLLOWING: a track may also carry path (path data in stage PERCENT, 0-100 on both axes: the motion_path grammar, M L H V C S Q T A Z, 700 characters), and keys with a (0-1, how far along it): the element's top-left rides the path, like x and y, and a track with a keys ignores its x and y. orient: true also turns the element to the path's direction (rotate keys on the same track are then ignored). trail: {n 1-6, lag 0.02-0.5 s} adds n fading copies of a top-level block (it needs a numeric place.w) that follow the same path a little later, each fainter and blurrier than the one before. SPRING: a key ease (which governs the segment arriving at that key) may also be {spring: {stiffness 1-1000 (default 170), damping 0-100 (default 26), mass 0.1-10 (default 1)}} or {spring: true} for the defaults: a damped spring, computed when the page is built (semi-implicit Euler, 1 ms step, time in seconds), so the player needs no extra script. The spring replaces the segment arriving at the key that carries it (previous key value to this one), written as 24 linear steps; the key is always exact and every other segment keeps its own ease. Pick values that settle within the segment, otherwise it snaps at this key. Under-damped springs overshoot (clamped to the property range). A first key with no previous key, or any other ease object, keeps the normal ease.

scenes.description: array (max 12) of {layer: id, t | beat, transition?}, optional. STITCHES scenes together: each layer (usually a motion_layer) is hidden until its start and hands over to the next scene instead of cutting. Within `overlap` seconds of the next scene's start the old one leaves while the new one arrives. transition is one of cut, dissolve, push, zoom-through, blur, rise, whip, wipe, iris, clock, slice, flip, spin, portal (with `portal: {x, y, w}`), ribbon, fade-through, shared-x, shared-y, shared-z, collapse and applies to the scene it names (the hand-over INTO it); without one the timeline's `stitch` is used. Your own tracks on the same layer are applied after these and win, so a scene can still do its own entrance.

morphs.description: array (max 6) of {from, to, t | beat, dur?, ease?} (optional). Match cut: a copy of the `from` child flies from its box to the `to` child's box (resizing on the way) starting at t, over dur seconds (0.1-4, default 0.8), with ease (a motion token, default quart-in-out). from hides when the flight starts and to appears when it lands, so the morph owns their opacity: do not also give them opacity tracks. Both must have a numeric place.w and sit at the top level or directly inside a motion_layer; others are dropped and reported.

stitch.description: "cut" | "dissolve" | "push" | "zoom-through" | "blur" | "rise" | "whip" | "wipe" | "iris" | "clock" | "slice" | "flip" | "spin" | "portal" | "ribbon" | "fade-through" | "shared-x" | "shared-y" | "shared-z" | "collapse" (optional, default "dissolve"). The four Material patterns fade the old scene out in the first 30% of the overlap and the new one in after it, so the two are never both half visible: fade-through brings the new scene up from 92% size, shared-x and shared-y slide it in along the axis (8% and 6% of the stage), shared-z scales it from 80% while the old one grows to 110%; set overlap to about 0.3 for the 300 ms Material uses. whip is a fast push with heavy motion blur; wipe reveals the new scene left to right over the old one; iris opens a circle from the centre; clock sweeps round like a clock hand; slice reveals through vertical bars; flip turns the old scene edge-on and the new one in; spin rotates and scales through; portal dives into a box in the old scene (give that scene entry `portal: {x, y, w}` in stage percent, the box keeps the stage shape) and the box becomes the new scene; without a box it falls back to dissolve; ribbon sweeps a slanted band in the accent colour across the frame and reveals the new scene behind it. The hand-over used by scenes that do not name one. collapse squeezes the OLD scene sideways to a thin vertical band that narrows to nothing (content clipped with it, over the overlap), and the new scene appears when that is done: a closing move, best before a blank beat or a lone object. Pick one per film: a shared motion vector between scenes is what reads as designed.

overlap.description: number (optional). Seconds a hand-over takes, 0-3. Default 0.6. Ignored by cut.

camera.description: {keys: [{t | beat, ease?, x?, y?, zoom?, rx?, ry?, rz?, z?}]} (max 48 keys), optional. z (-1500 to 1500 px) dollies the camera through depth: top-level blocks with place.depth (0-1) sit further back and, with a compensating scale, look unchanged at z 0, so moving z gives real parallax. x,y are the focus point in percent of the stage (default 50,50); zoom 0.25-6 (default 1); rx, ry, rz tilt in degrees. Moves only layer:"world" children.

Scrubbable, loopable, frame-exact.

motion_group.description: Blocks that enter one after another: a stagger, set once. Every child gets the same entrance (effect, ease, duration) offset by stagger milliseconds, on load or when scrolled into view. The general-purpose alternative to hand-setting a delay on each block; for a single block use the `enter` prop that any atom accepts.

ease.description: string | [x1,y1,x2,y2] (optional). A token from motion_tokens, or four numbers. Default depends on the effect (expo-out for most).

duration.description: integer | "instant" | "quick" | "base" | "slow" | "cinematic" (optional). Milliseconds 0-8000 or a duration token. Default 560.

delay.description: integer (optional). Milliseconds before the first child, 0-20000. Default 0.

on.description: "load" | "view" (optional, default "load"). "view" waits until the group is scrolled into view; without JavaScript it simply shows.

motion_group.x-routing-text: Blocks that enter one after another with a set stagger: the same entrance effect, ease and duration for every child, offset per child, on load or when scrolled into view.
x-intent-phrases: Have these cards appear one after another with a short stagger.
Fade and slide my list items in on load, expo-out, 80ms apart.
Reveal this section's blocks as the reader scrolls to them.

motion_tokens.description: The catalogue's motion vocabulary, drawn: every named easing curve with a dot riding it, the cubic-bezier it stands for and what it is for, the five duration tokens, and the nine entrance effects. The same names are accepted by the `enter` prop on any atom, by motion_group, by reveal, and by every ease field in motion_timeline, so an agent learns the vocabulary once. Honours prefers-reduced-motion (dots stay still).
motion_tokens.x-routing-text: Reference card for the catalogue's motion vocabulary: named easing curves (expo-out, standard, emphasized, quart-in-out, overshoot...) each drawn as a dot riding the curve with its cubic-bezier and its use, duration tokens, and entrance effects.
x-intent-phrases: Show me the easing curves I can use for UI animation and what each is for.
What motion tokens does this catalogue offer?
Give me a motion style guide for our design system.

motion_layer.description: A scene. Children are any atoms, placed in percent of THIS layer (place {x, y, w, h, z, origin}, id, exactly as inside a motion_timeline), and the whole layer moves as one: give the layer an id and fade, slide, scale or blur it with opacity, x, y, scale and blur tracks to cut between scenes. Use it inside a motion_timeline; a layer with no place fills the stage. Layers are what make a piece with several scenes cheap to author: one id per scene instead of one track per element.

blocks.description: array (max 24) of any atom blocks. Each may carry id (^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]{0,31}$), place {x, y, w, h, z, origin}. Ids must be unique across the whole timeline.

motion_text.description: Kinetic type. The text reveals unit by unit as p goes 0 to 1: per line, word or character (or all at once), with reveal "mask" (each unit slides up out of a clipped line, the signature designed look), "rise", "drop", "fade" or "blur". Sized in px on the stage, so the composition is identical at any width, and coloured from the stage theme unless a colour is given. Screen readers get the plain text. Standalone it renders fully revealed. Plain HTML and CSS, no script: it moves with the --p custom property that a motion_timeline p track sets, and standalone it renders its final state.

text.description: string (max 4 lines of 60 characters, 160 total; lines split on \n). Default "Text". A word between asterisks (*plan*) takes the accent colour, whichever way the text reveals; two asterisks in a row are a literal one.

font.description: "sans" | "serif" | "mono" | "display" (optional, default "sans"). display is a heavy grotesque.

mode.description: "lines" | "words" | "chars" | "block" (optional, default "lines"). What reveals in turn. lines never wraps; more than 120 units falls back to block.

reveal.description: "mask" | "rise" | "drop" | "fade" | "blur" | "bar" | "flap" | "reel" | "pop" | "decode" | "bloom" (optional, default "rise"). bloom condenses each unit in place out of a bright, glowing blur: it starts about 60% brighter with a soft halo and a 0.4em blur at 90% size, and halo, brightness and blur fall away as it sharpens (no slide; blur only defocuses, decode swaps glyphs, bloom adds the glow). Pair with a long overlap (4-8) and mode words or lines so the glow runs through the whole line. pop scales each unit up past full size and settles (an overshoot). decode shows seeded random characters that resolve into each unit (the real text is always in the page; the noise is aria-hidden). bar wipes a coloured highlight bar in behind each unit, then the text appears on it. flap is a slot-reel flip: three decoy glyphs scroll past in each unit before the real one lands (best with mode chars). reel stacks the lines on one row and the second dial (--s) moves the focus down the list: the focused line is sharp, the others dim, shrink and blur with their distance (a scrolling text reel); at --s 1 the last line is in focus.

overlap.description: integer (optional). How many units are mid-reveal at once, 1-8. Higher is softer. Default 3.

tracking.description: number (optional). Letter spacing in em, -0.1 to 0.5. Default -0.02.

accent.description: "#rrggbb" (optional). Colour of words wrapped in asterisks. Default the stage accent.

accent_gradient.description: ["#rrggbb", "#rrggbb"] (optional). Two colours that run across the accent words (the ones in asterisks) instead of the flat accent colour.

glow.description: integer (optional). A soft glow behind the type, 0-40 px. Default 0 (off).

glow_color.description: "#rrggbb" (optional). Colour of the glow. Default the accent.

shine.description: bool (optional). A band of light that sweeps across the letters as the second dial (--s) goes 0 to 1. Default false.

cycle.description: array (2-6) of strings, max 40 characters each (optional). Words that swap in place with a blur crossfade as the second dial (--s) goes 0 to 1, after the text (or on their own when text is empty): on your phone / the web / the terminal. Take the accent colour.

bar.description: "#rrggbb" (optional). Colour of the highlight bar for reveal "bar". Default the stage accent.

extrude.description: integer (optional). Depth in px of a solid 3D extrusion behind the type, 0-30. Default 0.

extrude_dir.description: "diagonal" | "down" (optional, default "diagonal"). Which way the extrusion falls.

decor.description: "strike" | "underline" | "highlight" (optional). A line that sweeps across each unit (line, word or character) in turn as the second dial (--s) goes 0 to 1: a strike-through (the text dims), an underline, or a marker highlight behind it. With no step track it shows finished.

karaoke.description: "pill" | "color" (optional). Lights each unit (use mode words) in turn as --s goes 0 to 1, as a pill behind it or a colour change: the animated caption. Nothing is lit at 0 or 1.

split.description: integer (optional). Red and cyan copies pull apart by this many px at the peak of --s and sit together at 0: the chromatic glitch. 0-60. Default 0 (off).

split_a.description: "#rrggbb" (optional). Left copy. Default a hot pink.

prism.description: array (2-4) of words, max 14 characters each (optional). A turning 3D prism after the text that cycles the words as the second dial (--s) goes 0 to 1 (one full turn): Build / Ship / Scale. Two words repeat to fill four faces. Needs at least two words, else ignored.

order.description: "forward" | "reverse" | "centre" | "random" (optional, default "forward"). The order units reveal in: reading order, last first, from the middle outwards, or a fixed random order (see order_seed). The step-dial effects (karaoke, decor, wave) keep reading order.

order_seed.description: integer (optional). 0-999. Seeds order random and the noise of reveal decode. Default 3.

accent_font.description: "sans" | "serif" | "mono" | "display" (optional). A typeface for the words wrapped in asterisks, so one word can be set in serif inside sans text. Default none (the line face).

accent_style.description: "italic" (optional). Sets the asterisk words in italic. Default none.

wave.description: integer (optional). Letters ride a travelling vertical wave of this many px as the second dial (--s) goes 0 to 1, flat at both ends. 0-40. Default 0 (off). Best with mode chars.

start_scale.description: number (optional). 1-12. The whole line starts this many times its size, cropped by the box, and shrinks to its size as p goes 0 to 1: the oversize zoom-down. Default 1 (off). The box hides what falls outside it.

caret.description: bool (optional). A caret follows the unit being revealed and stays on the last one. Use with mode words or chars; lines and block have no caret. Default false.

motion_shape.description: A form that draws or grows with p: a bar or rule (grow-x, grow-y), a disc (scale), a ring that sweeps round like a progress dial (sweep), or a fade; solid or a two-colour gradient at an angle, with rounded corners, and an optional heavy blur that makes it a soft glow behind everything. Fills its placed box, or w/h px. Plain HTML and CSS, no script: it moves with the --p custom property that a motion_timeline p track sets, and standalone it renders its final state.

fill2.description: "#rrggbb" (optional). Second colour; makes a gradient (for a ring, the sweep colour).

angle.description: integer (optional). Gradient angle in degrees, 0-360. Default 90.

thickness.description: integer (optional). Ring and line thickness px, 1-200. Default 6.

radius.description: integer (optional). Rect corner radius px, 0-500. Default 0.

draw.description: "grow-x" | "grow-y" | "scale" | "sweep" | "fade" | "none" (optional). Default grow-x for rect and line, scale for circle, sweep for ring. sweep is ring only. pulse (ring and circle only) is a ripple: the second dial (--s) goes 0 to 1 and the form swells and fades out, invisible at both ends.

lag.description: number (optional). With draw pulse, delays the ripple, 0-0.9 of the dial. Several rings with growing lag make concentric ripples. Default 0.

blur.description: integer (optional). Blur px, 0-200. A big blur on a gradient disc is an ambient glow. Default 0.

w.description: integer (optional). Width px, 1-3000. Default 100% of the placed box.

h.description: integer (optional). Height px, 1-3000. Default 100% of the placed box. A line is thickness tall.

motion_counter.description: A big number that counts from `from` to `to` as p goes 0 to 1, with thousands separators, prefix, suffix, fixed decimals and an optional small-caps caption under it. The generic form of a stat for any topic: nights, artists, kilometres, followers. Plain HTML and CSS, no script: it moves with the --p custom property that a motion_timeline p track sets, and standalone it renders its final state.

label_size.description: integer (optional). Caption px, 8-80. Default a fifth of size.

roll.description: bool (optional). Odometer: every digit is a 0-9 strip that scrolls to its value, left to right, as p goes 0 to 1. Counts from zero (from is ignored). Default false.

motion_pill.description: A rounded call-to-action chip: "Comment *Motion* under this post". The words between asterisks take the accent colour (two asterisks in a row are a literal one), with an optional leading glyph. It fades and rises with p, and put in a layer with layer:"hud" it stays on screen across every scene and camera move, the way social films keep their ask visible. Plain HTML and CSS, no script: it moves with the --p custom property a motion_timeline p track sets, and standalone it renders its final state.

text.description: string (max 60). Default "Label". *word* takes the accent colour; ** is a literal asterisk.

icon.description: string (optional, max 2). A glyph before the text, in the accent colour.

color.description: "#rrggbb" (optional). Text colour. Default the stage ink.

fill.description: "#rrggbb" (optional). Chip fill. Default a faint tint of the stage ink.

border_gradient.description: ["#rrggbb", "#rrggbb"] (optional). A two-colour gradient outline instead of the faint line.

glow.description: integer (optional). A soft glow around the chip, 0-40 px, in the gradient colours or the accent. Default 0 (off).

href.description: string (optional). Makes the pill a real link: https, mailto or a relative path; anything else is dropped. Default none.

motion_checklist.description: A card of items that tick off one after another as p goes 0 to 1: each row brightens and slides in while its check pops, with optional empty placeholder rows under the real ones (the "recipe" card: your knowledge, your process, your automations). Plain HTML and CSS, no script: it moves with the --p custom property a motion_timeline p track sets, and standalone it renders every item ticked.

items.description: array (max 6) of string or {text, icon?} (text max 40, icon max 2 characters). Default one item "Item".

skeleton.description: integer (optional). Empty placeholder rows under the items, 0-4. Default 0.

accent.description: "#rrggbb" (optional). Colour of the ticks. Default the stage accent.

motion_orbit.description: Tiles that fly out from the centre onto an ellipse as p goes 0 to 1, then swing round it as step goes 0 to 1: the ring of app icons around a product shot. Tiles are text (a letter, a glyph or a short label), never brand logos, so there is nothing to license. Place it over the same box as the thing it surrounds. Uses CSS cos() and sin(), so it needs a current browser. Plain HTML and CSS, no script; standalone it renders the tiles in place.

items.description: array (max 12) of string or {text}; text max 8 characters (one or two reads as a glyph, longer as a small label), or max 24 with shape pill.

shape.description: "pill" (optional). Rectangular pill tiles that size to their label (text up to 24 characters, one line, no wrapping) instead of square tiles. Anything else keeps the square tile and the 8-character limit. Tile height is 55% of size, so size sets the pill height; allow room around the ring for long labels.

rx.description: integer (optional). Horizontal radius, percent of the placed box, 5-60. Default 40.

ry.description: integer (optional). Vertical radius, percent of the placed box, 5-60. Default 36.

start.description: integer (optional). Angle of the first tile in degrees, -360 to 360. Default -90 (top).

spin.description: integer (optional). Degrees the ring turns as step goes 0 to 1, -360 to 360. Default 40.

ring.description: bool (optional). A faint dashed ellipse behind the tiles. Default true.

motion_code.description: A code window that types itself in as p goes 0 to 1: monospace lines revealed left to right in order with a caret on the line being typed, keywords in the accent colour and // comments dimmed. No script and no per-letter markup, because a line's width is its character count in ch. For show, not for syntax highlighting. Standalone it renders all the code.

lines.description: array (max 14) of string (max 72 characters each). Blank strings are blank lines.

file.description: string (optional, max 32). Shown in the window bar.

accent.description: "#rrggbb" (optional). Keywords and caret. Default the stage accent.

motion_mark.description: The catalogue's own mark (three tilted ellipses around a nucleus, one electron) that draws itself as p goes 0 to 1 and whose electron circles its orbit as step goes 0 to 1. The opening frame of a film or a brand sting. Geometry is the site logo's; the two colours are fields. Plain SVG and CSS, no script: it moves with the --p and --s custom properties a motion_timeline p and step track set, and standalone it renders the finished mark.

size.description: integer (optional). Width and height px, 24-600. Default 120.

accent.description: "#rrggbb" (optional). Two ellipses and the nucleus. Default the stage accent.

accent2.description: "#rrggbb" (optional). The third ellipse and the electron. Default "#00b7c3".

motion_browser.description: The catalogue browser, as a shot: a search box that types its query, filter chips with a count, and a grid of cards that rise in, each holding a LIVE render of a real atom (give the atom block as the card's preview) with its name, description, surface badge and source. One card can be picked: it lifts and takes an accent outline as step goes 0 to 1. p 0 to 0.3 types the query, p 0.3 to 1 brings the cards in. Use it to show a library of components honestly, with real names, real descriptions and real renders, instead of a mock-up. Plain HTML and CSS, no script; standalone it renders the finished screen.

query.description: string (optional, max 16). Typed into the search box as p goes 0 to 0.3.

placeholder.description: string (optional, max 24). Shown before typing starts. Default "Search atoms...".

chips.description: array (max 6) of string (max 24). The first is drawn active.

cards.description: array (max 6) of {title (max 28), text (max 90), badge? (max 16), source? (max 20), preview? (an atom block, rendered live)}.

pick.description: integer (optional). Index of the card to lift and outline as step goes 0 to 1, -1 for none. Default -1.

well.description: "#rrggbb" (optional). Background of the preview area of each card. Real atoms are drawn for their own surfaces and some hard-code dark text, so on a dark stage give them a light well. Default none.

accent.description: "#rrggbb" (optional). Search border, active chip, picked card. Default the stage accent.

motion_sketch.description: Strokes that draw themselves one after another as p goes 0 to 1, like an agent sketching: each stroke is path data (M, L, H, V, C, S, Q, T, A, Z with numbers; anything else and the stroke is dropped), drawn in a chosen colour and width, optionally with a soft fill that appears as it is drawn. Not raw SVG markup, so nothing but a path can reach the page. Sized by a viewBox (w by h, default 400 by 400) and scaled to its placed box. Plain SVG and CSS, no script: it moves with the --p custom property a motion_timeline p track sets, and standalone it renders the finished drawing.

strokes.description: array (max 24) of {d, color?, width?, fill?, fill_opacity?}. d is path data (max 700 characters of path commands, numbers and separators). color and fill are "#rrggbb"; width 1-24 px (default 6); fill_opacity 0-1 (default 0.2). Strokes draw in order.

label.description: string (optional, max 60). Accessible name of the drawing. Default "Sketch".

trim.description: object (optional) {start, end, offset}, like After Effects trim paths. start and end are 0-1 of each stroke's length (defaults 0 and 1) and bound the part that is drawn; offset -1 to 1 shifts the window along the stroke (a window pushed past the end wraps round to the start). The window draws on as p goes 0 to 1 (from start to end). end at or below start draws no stroke. Absent, empty or all defaults: the full stroke, unchanged.

motion_leader.description: A callout line that draws itself from one point to another as p goes 0 to 1: straight or bent, with a start dot, an arrowhead that lands at the end, and a label that fades in beside the tip. The annotation that points at a part of a diagram, a map or a product shot. Points are in viewBox units (w by h, default 400 by 300) and the whole thing scales to its placed box. Plain SVG and CSS, no script: it moves with the --p custom property a motion_timeline p track sets, and standalone it renders finished.

from.description: [x, y] (optional). Start point in viewBox units. Default [48, 210] on the default 400 by 300 box.

to.description: [x, y] (optional). End point, where the arrowhead lands. Default [352, 90].

curve.description: integer (optional). Bend, -100 to 100, as a percentage of the line length at its middle. 0 is straight. Default 0.

label.description: string (optional, max 40). Text beside the tip.

dot.description: bool (optional). Dot at the start. Default true.

color.description: "#rrggbb" (optional). Line, dot and arrowhead. Default the stage accent.

motion_mask.description: Reveals its child blocks through a shape that grows as p goes 0 to 1: a wobbly blob, a circle, a diagonal wipe, a rounded rectangle that opens, venetian bars, a diamond, a halftone dot grid, a conic sweep, or horizontal slats. The scene that opens out of a cloud-shaped hole, or the screenshot that wipes in. The blob and circle are 20-vertex polygons whose coordinates use CSS cos() and sin(), so they need no script and a current browser. At p = 1 the child is fully visible; standalone it renders fully revealed.

d.description: string (optional, max 4000 characters; used only when shape is "path"). An SVG path of straight and curve commands (M L H V C S Q T Z, absolute or relative; no arcs A, no exponent numbers, numbers up to 1000000). Only the first subpath is used. It is flattened, resampled to 48 points and stretched to fill the box, then scales in from the centre as p goes 0 to 1 (a 48-vertex clip polygon, pure CSS); at p = 1 the child shows through the whole shape. A missing or invalid d, or one that covers less than 1% of the box (a straight line), is ignored with an HTML comment and the blob is used. Absent: unchanged.

blocks.description: array (max 6) of any atom blocks, revealed together. Each may carry an id a timeline track can address.

motion_envelope.description: An envelope that carries a letter. Children are ordinary atoms shown on the letter card. With mode open, the flap flips up and the letter rises out as p goes 0 to 1; with mode seal, the letter drops in, the flap closes and the stamp lands. Optional address line (to) and stamp text. Plain HTML and CSS, no script; standalone it renders the finished state (open: letter out; seal: sealed and stamped). Use inside a motion_timeline to show a message being packed or delivered, e.g. an A2UI payload wrapped as an MCP tool result.

width.description: integer (optional). Envelope width px, 80-900; height is 5/8 of it. Default 360.

blocks.description: array (max 3) of atom blocks shown on the letter. They render finished (they do not follow the envelope's p).

to.description: string (optional, max 60). Address line on the front, e.g. "ui://jobs/board".

stamp.description: string (optional, max 24). Stamp text, e.g. "tool result". In seal mode it lands at the end.

fill.description: "#rrggbb" (optional). Envelope colour. Default a tint of the stage background.

accent.description: "#rrggbb" (optional). Fold edges and stamp. Default the stage accent.

color.description: "#rrggbb" (optional). Address text. Default the stage ink.

motion_rays.description: A sunburst that fans out behind a hero as p goes 0 to 1 (kind burst, --s turns it), or horizontal speed streaks that sweep across the frame (kind speed, --s slides them). Plain CSS gradients, no script; standalone it renders finished.

angle.description: integer (optional). Kind speed only: the direction the lines run, in degrees clockwise from horizontal, -180 to 180. Default 0 (horizontal lines streaming left to right as step advances). The lines and their travel turn together inside the same 16:9 frame, clipped to it. Ignored by burst; 0 or a non-number keeps the horizontal look exactly.

thickness.description: number (optional). Share of each step that is ray, 0.1-0.9. Default 0.5.

spin.description: integer (optional). Degrees turned at --s = 1 (burst), -360 to 360. Default 45.

motion_hud.description: A heads-up display that fills its placed box: corner brackets, a timecode that counts up from 0 to `seconds` as p goes 0 to 1, a label top right and a progress bar along the bottom. The recording-viewfinder look. Plain HTML and CSS; the timecode is rewritten by the timeline clock like motion_counter.

seconds.description: integer (optional). Where the timecode ends, 1-3600. Default 10.

label.description: string (optional, max 30). Top right, e.g. REC.

motion_lower_third.description: A lower third: an accent bar draws, the name slides out of it behind a clip, and the role fades in under it as p goes 0 to 1. Plain CSS, no script; standalone it renders finished.

accent.description: "#rrggbb" (optional). Bar and role. Default the stage accent.

motion_finish.description: A finishing layer for the whole frame, like a colourist: film grain (fixed seeded noise, drifting with --s), a vignette, warm or cool light leaks that drift, and an optional glass sheen that sweeps across with p. Place it last and full size (place 0,0,100,100); it never takes clicks. p fades it in. Plain SVG and CSS, no script.

sheen.description: bool (optional). A diagonal highlight band sweeping across with p. Default false.

motion_arch.description: An architecture diagram that draws itself on the film clock. Nodes (device, app, server, tool, model, store, surface, user) pop in, edges draw box edge to box edge with arrowheads and labels, and messages, the payloads that actually move, ride the edges as chips (back true for the reply). Each element has a window [at, at + dur] of the progress p a motion_timeline track drives; standalone it is the finished diagram. Pure SVG and CSS, no script.

nodes.description: array (max 12) of {id, kind?, label, sub?, x, y, w?, h?, at?, dur?}. id ^[a-z][a-z0-9_-]{0,31}$. kind "device" | "app" | "server" | "tool" | "model" | "store" | "surface" | "user" (default "server") sets the glyph and tint. x, y are the centre in percent of the frame; w, h percent (default 20 and 15). at, dur are the appearance window in p (0-1).

edges.description: array (max 16) of {from, to, label?, label2?, style?, both?, curve?, points?, label_at?, color?, at?, dur?}. from and to are node ids. style "solid" (draws on) | "dashed" (fades in). both adds a second arrowhead. curve -100 to 100 bends it. points (optional, max 10) is the edge's own route, a list of {x, y} in percent of the frame from the first box's rim to the second's: it is drawn as a polyline with rounded corners (see radius) instead of the curve, the arrowhead follows the last segment, and messages ride the route. label_at (optional) {x, y} in percent is where the centre of the label goes (default: above the middle of the route or curve); a routed edge's label is drawn above the message chips. Numbers only; an invalid points or label_at is ignored. label (max 48) is the text on the edge; label2 (optional, max 48, drawn only when label is set) is a second line under it, so a long label can wrap onto two lines instead of being cut.

messages.description: array (max 12) of {edge, text, back?, color?, at?, dur?}. edge is an index into edges; text (max 40) is the payload chip; back true sends it from the edge's end to its start.

groups.description: array (max 4) of {label, x, y, w, h, at?, dur?}: dashed boundaries in percent of the frame.

radius.description: integer (optional). Corner radius px of edges that have points, 0-60. Default 10. Never more than half of a segment.

accent.description: "#rrggbb" (optional). Device, app and surface nodes, and messages. Default the stage accent.

accent2.description: "#rrggbb" (optional). Server and tool nodes, and edges. Default "#2ac4ce".

color.description: "#rrggbb" (optional). Label ink. Default the stage ink.

background.description: "#rrggbb" (optional). Halo behind edge labels; match the stage. Default "#1e2733".

label.description: string (optional, max 80). Accessible name. Default "Architecture diagram".

motion_video.description: A muted video on the film clock. Inside a motion_timeline a track drives its progress p from 0 to 1 and the video seeks to from + p * (to - from), so scrubbing and frame export are exact; standalone it plays muted and loops. Made for screen recordings inside motion_device, with the motion design around them. Encode with short keyframe intervals for smooth seeking.

url.description: string. https URL or a /-rooted path to an mp4 or webm (no data URLs). Otherwise a placeholder shows.

poster.description: string (optional). https URL or /-rooted image path shown before the first frame.

from.description: number (optional). Seconds into the video at p = 0, 0-3600. Default 0.

to.description: number (optional). Seconds at p = 1, 0-3600. Default the end of the video.

still.description: bool (optional). Standalone, hold the first frame instead of playing. Default false.

motion_shader.description: A WebGL shader background: a domain-warped liquid gradient (kind liquid), soft aurora bands (kind aurora) or folded satin with a moving sheen (kind silk) in three colours. Seekable: shader time follows the film, read from the second dial (--s) every frame, so a step track drives it and seeking shows exactly that frame (span = shader seconds per unit of --s); standalone it runs on its own clock, or holds still with still true or under reduced motion. The shader and its driver are fixed in the renderer and the config is numbers only, so nothing in the payload becomes code. Its own CSS gradient of the same colours is the fallback when WebGL is missing, the shader fails, the page prints or the host strips scripts. p fades it in. Preview: a spike to judge whether WebGL earns a place.

kind.description: "liquid" | "aurora" | "silk" | "dots" | "vortex" (optional, default "liquid"). dots: a halftone wave, a grid of dots whose size swells and fades in waves (color1 the ground, color2 and color3 the dots). vortex: dots arranged in a spiral tunnel that recedes to the centre and turns with time. silk: satin folds lit from their own surface, color1 the shadowed cloth, color2 the lit cloth, color3 the sheen.

span.description: number (optional). Shader seconds per unit of --s, 0-600. Default 20.

still.description: bool (optional). Standalone, hold a still frame. Default false.

fill.description: bool (optional). Fill the placed box height instead of using ratio. Default false.

motion_bricks.description: A toy-brick sculpture on the film clock: procedural boxes with real brick proportions, studs, shadows and instruction-style edges (the brick_build_3d engine, here with boxes only; real LDraw parts are brick_build_3d's partsModel), drawn on a transparent stage so it sits inside a film. Bricks drop into place in build order as p goes 0 to 1 (p 1 = every brick settled) and the model turns with the second dial (--s, turns per unit), so a step track spins it and seeking shows exactly that frame. Give text to set a word in bricks (each character of a 5x7 dot font, every row merged into 1x1 to 1x4 bricks, depth studs deep), bricks for an explicit model, or a named shape. The optional motion object sets how the bricks arrive: the order they launch in, where they fly in from, how long each flight lasts, how much they tumble, and a small overshoot and recoil as they seat; all of it is numbers and fixed names that are clamped, and a stud-cell pass keeps a brick from launching before the brick it rests on. Standalone it shows the finished model. The engine is fixed code and the config is numbers, colours and the brick list, so nothing in the payload becomes code; without WebGL the engine draws with a 2D canvas painter instead. Known limit: each brick canvas holds two WebGL contexts and a page allows about 16, so keep to about 7 brick canvases per page. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the LEGO Group. LEGO is a trademark of the LEGO Group.

text.description: string (optional, max 12). Builds the word in bricks: A-Z, 0-9 and . , ! ? - : ' (others leave a gap).

bricks.description: array (optional). Explicit toy-brick model (procedural boxes, up to 3000), same format as brick_build_3d: {x, y, z, w, d, h, c} or [x, y, z, w, d, c] / [x, y, z, w, d, h, c]. Used when text is absent.

shape.description: string (optional). One of "heart", "sphere", "torus", "helix", "pyramid", "house". Default "heart". Used when neither text nor bricks is given.

color.description: string (optional). A "#rrggbb" colour. One colour for every lettering brick; otherwise letters cycle through palette or the classic brick colours.

depth.description: integer (optional). Lettering depth in studs, 1-4. Default 2.

base.description: string (optional). "none" for floating bricks (no plate, no plate shadow), or a "#rrggbb" colour for the baseplate. Default the classic green plate.

look.description: string (optional). One of "studio", "instructions". Default "studio". studio: a product shot (glossy ABS, softbox reflections, edges that catch light, no outlines). instructions: the building-instructions style of brick_build_3d (dark edge lines).

angle.description: number (optional). Starting turn in degrees, -360 to 360. Default 24.

motion.description: object (optional). How the bricks arrive; absent = the plain build-up. Every key is optional and clamped, unknown keys are ignored, and a value that is not a number or a known name falls back to its default. order: "index" (the brick list order) | "base-up" (layer by layer) | "diagonal" | "radial" (default "diagonal"). from: "above" | "outward" | "scatter" (where bricks start; default "above"). spinAxis: "y" | "x" | "z" (default "y"). window: 0-30, default 2.4, how widely the launch times are spread. flight: 0.1-5, default 0.62, how long one brick is in the air; together they set the pace, since p 0 to 1 covers window + flight. distance: 0-60, default 9, start distance in stud units. tilt: 0-360, default 70, random start tumble in degrees. spin: -8 to 8, default 0.5, extra turns while flying. gravity: 0-1, default 0.5, how strongly lower bricks go first (diagonal and radial orders). jitter: 0-1, default 0.15, random shuffle of the order. support: 0 or 1, default 1, a brick never launches before the brick it rests on. seed: integer 0-2147483646, default 7. overshoot 0-1 (0.12), rotOvershoot 0-0.5 (0.08), recoil 0-1 (0.45), travel 0.2-0.9 (0.58), sharpness 1.5-8 (4): the seat-and-settle curve. direction: [x, y, z], default [1, 0.55, 0.8], the sweep direction for the diagonal order.

agent_sketchpad.description: A single composite SVG canvas built from an ORDERED list of validated SVG elements, for an agent to progressively draw one coherent picture across multiple real updates (e.g. one A2A message per shape) rather than svg_path_draw's one-shot single shape. Every re-render draws all elements except the last as already-complete (no animation); only the LAST element in the list gets the real stroke-dasharray/stroke-dashoffset draw-in animation -- a stateless rule that works under this catalogue's full-rerender model without any incremental DOM patching. Redesigned 2026-08-24 from a path-only shape to a general SVG-primitive one (with fill), to match what a real freeform tool-calling loop actually produces (see streaming-testbench's demos/sketch/sketch_agent.py, the origin of this atom's validation approach) -- works anywhere svg_path_draw does.

strokes.description: array of {element, label?} (required). ORDERED -- element is RAW SVG MARKUP for exactly ONE element (real creative freedom within a fixed safety allowlist, not a raw pass-through): one of circle, ellipse, rect, line, polyline, polygon, path, g (g may nest further allowed elements). Allowed attributes: cx, cy, r, rx, ry, x, y, width, height, x1, y1, x2, y2, points, d, fill, stroke, stroke-width, opacity, fill-opacity, stroke-opacity, stroke-linecap, stroke-linejoin, transform -- attribute values are restricted to a safe alphanumeric/punctuation character class (blocks javascript:, event handlers, anything script-shaped). The renderer parses and re-validates every element server-side before embedding it (never trusts the string as-is) -- an element that fails validation (disallowed tag/attribute, unsafe value, malformed markup, more than one top-level element) is skipped with a console warning, not a crash. label is an optional short phrase describing that one element (e.g. "the lighthouse tower"), not rendered, useful for an agent-facing tool-call log. Resend the FULL, growing array on every update (A2UI messages carry full values, not deltas) -- only the LAST item in the array animates; everything before it renders as already-drawn. Capped defensively at 250 elements and 4096 raw markup characters per element by the renderer (over-cap elements are skipped with a console warning, not a crash).

viewBox.description: string (optional). SVG viewBox, e.g. "0 0 400 200". Default "0 0 400 200" -- pick a canvas shape that fits what's being drawn, unlike svg_path_draw's fixed 400x80 box.

brick_build_3d.description: Equation-driven toy-brick 3D model that assembles itself stud by stud, drawn in real brick proportions (8 mm pitch, 9.6 mm brick) with dependency-free WebGL — key-light shadows cast between parts, glossy plastic shading and an outline on every part edge, like an instruction-booklet render — and a canvas-2D fallback where WebGL is unavailable. Two kinds of model. Toy bricks (bricks or shape) are procedural boxes with studs, from a named shape (heart, sphere, torus, helix, pyramid, house) or an explicit bricks array. Real parts (partsModel) are baked geometry from the LDraw.org Parts Library, under CC BY. Every design is checked by deterministic geometry — collisions, every brick anchored through stud connections (real parts also through pins, hinges, axles and clips), connection count, centre of mass over the footprint — and the verdicts show beside the model. An instructions mode steps through the build layer by layer, and a parts list groups bricks by size and colour with an indicative cost. Known limit, each brick canvas holds two WebGL contexts and a page allows about 16, so keep to about 7 brick canvases per page. Not affiliated with or endorsed by the LEGO Group. LEGO is a trademark of the LEGO Group.

shape.description: string (optional). One of "heart", "sphere", "torus", "helix", "pyramid", "house". Default "heart". Ignored when bricks is set.

bricks.description: array (optional). Explicit model — objects {x, y, z, w, d, h, c}. x and z are stud positions, y is the layer (0 sits on the baseplate), w and d the footprint in studs, h the height in bricks (default 1), c a '#rrggbb' colour or a palette index. A brick may also be a compact array [x, y, z, w, d, c] or [x, y, z, w, d, h, c], about a third of the size. Up to 3000 bricks. A data-model binding such as {path '/bricks'} arrives resolved.

palette.description: array of "#rrggbb" (optional). Up to 256 colours. A brick's c may be an integer index into it, which keeps large models small.

step.description: integer (optional). Initial instruction step when mode is steps. Default 1.

orbit.description: boolean (optional). Slow auto-orbit; dragging always orbits. Default true.

height.description: integer (optional). Canvas height px, 160 to 900. Default 380.

bg.description: string (optional). Canvas background colour. Transparent on the studio gradient by default.

scrubber.description: boolean (optional). Show the animate/instructions toggle and step slider. Default true.

checks.description: boolean (optional). Show the build-check verdicts. Default true.

parts.description: boolean (optional). Show the parts list with an indicative cost. Default false.

models.description: array (optional). Named models for the picker dropdown — up to 8 objects {name, bricks, palette}, each bricks array as above (up to 3000 bricks each; palette optional, else the top-level one). Entries with no usable bricks are skipped; a missing name becomes Model N. The dropdown lists the six built-in shapes followed by these.

model.description: string (optional). Name of the entry in models to show first. Ignored when bricks is set.

picker.description: boolean (optional). Show the model dropdown. Default true when models is given, otherwise false; set true to get a dropdown of the six built-in shapes alone.

partsModel.description: array (optional). Real parts from the LDraw.org Parts Library (CC BY) instead of procedural boxes, as [partId, x, y, z, rotation, colour] tuples (a real LDraw part id, x y z in LDraw units (20 per stud, 24 per brick height), a 0-23 rotation index, an LDraw colour code), or objects {p, x, y, z, r, c}. Takes precedence over bricks/shape when present, same "explicit wins" rule as bricks vs. shape. Up to 3000 parts.

look.description: string (optional). One of "studio", "instructions". Default "instructions". instructions: the original building-instructions style (glossy plastic, dark outline on every part edge). studio: a product-shot style — no outlines, edges catch light instead (same visual treatment as the sibling motion_bricks atom, default there).

base.description: string (optional). "none" for floating bricks (no plate, no plate shadow), or a "#rrggbb" colour for the baseplate. Default the classic green plate.

spring_nodes.description: Mass-spring graph: nodes repel each other (Coulomb) and are held by Hooke springs on defined edges. By default a settled, static layout computed server-side, so it works everywhere, including print and assistive tech. Drag-to-pin with live springs is opt-in with interactive: true.

nodes.description: array (optional). Array of {id, label} objects. Defaults to 6 labelled nodes.

edges.description: array (optional). Array of {a, b} index pairs for spring connections.

colour.description: string (optional). Node and edge accent colour. Default

height.description: integer (optional). Canvas height px. Default 420.

rest_length.description: integer (optional). Spring rest length px. Default 110.

interactive.description: boolean (optional). Default false: a settled, static layout that works everywhere and for assistive tech. Set true when the atom is shown in a live browser or app view and the viewer should be able to play with the graph: drag nodes to pin them, watch the springs react. Ignored under reduced motion and on static surfaces (print, slides, email, chat, and any surface that strips scripts).
